doc.title: Ramsey Lewis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Listening to world music
summary: Lewis says he stays with American music through the African-American experience.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: But we at least identify what the problems are, and maybe through that we can continue dialoguing and sharing this with others, as we’re doing now. What I wanted to ask you: are you listening to any other music around the world. I know you . . .

No. I mean, I have music from various places around the world, but have I studied by sitting down and saying, “Let’s see what they’re doing? How can I use it?” No, I’m still dealing with American music by way of the African-American experience.
